name: booleans.minkowski
description: Compute the Minkowski sum of two 3D geometries. The Minkowski sum A ⊕ B is the set of all points a + b where a ∈ A and b ∈ B. Geometrically, this "inflates" geometry A by the shape of geometry B. Common use cases: - Offset a solid by a sphere to round all edges and corners - Offset a solid by a cube to create chamfered edges - Collision detection (if Minkowski sum contains origin, shapes overlap) For best performance, use convex geometries. Non-convex geometries are supported when the second operand is convex, but require decomposition and are slower.

params.name: geometries
params.description: two geom3 geometries (second should be convex for non-convex first)

name: booleans.scission
description: Scission (divide) the given geometry into the component pieces. NOTE: Currently only 3D geometries are supported.
example:
let figure = require('./my.stl')
let pieces = scission(figure)

name: booleans.subtract
description: Return a new geometry representing space in the first geometry but not in all subsequent geometries. The given geometries should be of the same type, either geom2 or geom3.

name: booleans.union
description: Return a new geometry representing the total space in the given geometries. The given geometries should be of the same type, either geom2 or geom3.

name: minkowski.minkowskiSum
description: Compute the Minkowski sum of two 3D geometries. The Minkowski sum A ⊕ B is the set of all points a + b where a ∈ A and b ∈ B. Geometrically, this "inflates" geometry A by the shape of geometry B. Common use cases: - Offset a solid by a sphere to round all edges and corners - Offset a solid by a cube to create chamfered edges - Collision detection (if Minkowski sum contains origin, shapes overlap) For best performance, use convex geometries. Non-convex geometries are supported when the second operand is convex, but require decomposition and are slower.

description: Create the outline(s) of the given geometry.

name: geometries.path2.appendBezier
description: Append a series of points to the given geometry that represent a Bezier curve. The Bézier curve starts at the last point in the given geometry, and ends at the last control point. The other control points are intermediate control points to transition the curve from start to end points. The first control point may be null to ensure a smooth transition occurs. In this case, the second to last point of the given geometry is mirrored into the control points of the Bezier curve. In other words, the trailing gradient of the geometry matches the new gradient of the curve.

options.name: controlPoints
options.description: list of control points (2D) for the bezier curve

options.name: segment
options.description: number of segments per 360 rotation

params.name: geometry
params.description: the path of which to appended points

name: geometries.path2.concat
description: Concatenate the given paths. If both contain the same point at the junction, merge it into one. A concatenation of zero paths is an empty, open path. A concatenation of one closed path to a series of open paths produces a closed path. A concatenation of a path to a closed path is an error.

description: Extrude a solid from slices that a callback places along the way; the default callback extrudes the shape one unit up Z.
example:

})

name: jscadText.init
description: Initialize jscad-text with a JSCAD modeling instance. The jscadui runtime does this with the @jscad/modeling it serves before model code runs, so a model needs no init; calling it again is harmless. Elsewhere, call it before text2d().

name: jscadText.text2d
description: Render text as 2D filled geometry (geom2), compatible with OpenSCAD text() semantics.

options.name: text
options.description: text to render (or first arg)

options.name: size
options.description: cap height in user units (matches OpenSCAD size)

options.name: font
options.description: omit for the Hershey stroke font. A font name, "Family" or "Family:style=Style" (e.g. "Liberation Sans:style=Bold"); an unknown name throws, listing the names. Also a TTF/OTF URL or file path, or the font file's bytes. Font names: Arial (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Arial Black, Calibri (Bold, Italic), Courier (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Courier New (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Georgia (Bold, Italic), Helvetica (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Impact, Inconsolata (Bold), Lato (Bold, Italic), Liberation Mono (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Liberation Sans (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Liberation Serif (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), monospace (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Montserrat (Bold, Italic), Noto Sans (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Open Sans (Bold, Italic), Oswald (Bold), Palatino Linotype (Bold), Roboto (Bold, Italic), sans-serif (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), serif (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Source Code Pro (Bold), Tahoma (Bold), Times (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Times New Roman (Bold, Italic, Bold Italic), Trebuchet MS (Bold, Italic), Ubuntu (Bold, Italic), Verdana (Bold, Italic)

options.name: halign
options.description: 'left' | 'center' | 'right'

options.name: valign
options.description: 'baseline' | 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom'

options.name: spacing
options.description: character spacing multiplier

options.name: direction
options.description: 'ltr' | 'rtl' (rtl: reverses text)

options.name: $fn
options.description: curve tessellation quality for TTF fonts

options.name: strokeWidth
options.description: Hershey stroke width (default: size*0.12)

params.name: textOrOptions
params.description: text string, or options object with `text` property

example:
const jscadText = require('@jscadui/jscad-text')
const outline = jscadText.text2d('HELLO', { size: 10, font: 'Liberation Sans:style=Bold', halign: 'center', valign: 'center' })

name: jscadText.text2dAsync
description: Render text using a TTF/OTF font asynchronously. The font is loaded and cached; subsequent calls with the same font are sync via text2d() once the font is in cache.

name: jscadText.isClockwise
description: Determine if a contour is clockwise (hole) via the shoelace formula. In OpenType fonts: outer contours are CCW, holes are CW.

name: jscadText.computeValignOffset
description: Compute the Y offset to apply to glyph geometry for the requested valign. The offset shifts the geometry so that y=0 aligns with the valign anchor. Add this offset to all glyph y-coordinates after layout.

name: jscadText.resolveFont
description: Resolve a font name or URL to a loadable source.

params.name: nameOrUrl
params.description: font name (e.g. "Liberation Sans") or direct URL/path

name: jscadText.registerFonts
description: Add or override entries in the runtime font map.

name: jscadText.registerFontFile
description: Parse a font file and register it under its own family and style names, replacing any existing entry of the same name. The parsed font is stored in the map, so later text2d calls reuse it without parsing again.

name: jscadText.registerNodeFont
description: Register a local file path as a cached version of a CDN URL. Called by fontCache.js once it has a local copy of the URL's file.

name: jscadText.listFonts
description: Get a read-only snapshot of all currently registered font names.

name: jscadText.fontList
description: Describe font map names as their families, each with its styles.

name: jscadText.loadSystemFonts
description: Discover and register system-installed fonts. - In Chrome 103+: uses the Local Font Access API (window.queryLocalFonts) - In Node.js: parses output of `fc-list` (fontconfig, Linux/Mac) Safe to call multiple times; only runs once. Does not throw - missing permissions or fc-list are silently ignored.
